name: İsmail Ogan
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver medal at the 1957 World Wrestling Championships in Istanbul at age 24, followed by World Cup gold in 1958 and World Championship bronze in 1959.
early_history_summary: Born into a nomadic Yörük family in Aksu, Antalya, Ogan began oil wrestling at age 9 to earn money for school supplies. He was discovered by national team coach Yaşar Doğu at the 1955 Elmalı oil wrestling festival and invited to Ankara to train in Olympic freestyle wrestling, quickly rising to the national team.
family_context_summary: Born to a nomadic Yörük (Honamlı) family in Aksu, Antalya; father was a camel and goat shepherd. The family lived in extreme poverty, and Ogan started wrestling at age 9 to afford notebook paper for school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a shepherd with no known wrestling background.
evidence_summary: Ogan grew up in extreme poverty in a nomadic Yörük family, starting oil wrestling at age 9 to buy school supplies. He was discovered by legendary national team coach Yaşar Doğu at 22 and trained under elite coaches Doğu and Celal Atik. His World Championship silver in 1957 at age 24 marked his arrival on the international stage, followed by World Cup gold in 1958 and Olympic silver in 1960.
starting_point: Born to a nomadic Yörük shepherd family in Aksu, Antalya, Turkey; extreme poverty, father was a camel and goat herder.
current_position: Died April 26, 2022 at age 89 in Antalya, Turkey; final role: retired Olympic champion wrestler and wrestling coach.

trajectory.event: Won silver medal at the World Wrestling Championships in Istanbul, his first major international medal.

name: Thomas Anders
milestone_by_age_26: As lead singer of Modern Talking, the debut single 'You're My Heart, You're My Soul' reached #1 in 35 countries in 1985, selling over 8 million copies worldwide.
early_history_summary: Born Bernd Weidung in Koblenz, West Germany, Anders began performing at age 6 and won a singing contest at 10, earning 300+ performances at a local music hall. After several failed Schlager singles, he was paired with producer Dieter Bohlen in 1983 to form Modern Talking, whose Eurodisco debut became a global smash hit in 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in Koblenz, West Germany; father was a civil servant at the local revenue service, mother ran a convenience store. Middle-class family that supported his early music interests with piano and singing lessons.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in the music industry, but supported his musical training from a young age with lessons and performance opportunities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dieter Bohlen partnership,Eurodisco wave,300+ childhood performances,record label access
evidence_summary: Anders grew up in a middle-class German family with supportive parents who funded music lessons. He performed over 300 times at a local music hall from age 10, building significant stage experience. His career breakthrough came from the complementary partnership with producer Dieter Bohlen in Modern Talking, riding the 1980s Eurodisco wave to global success with 'You're My Heart, You're My Soul' in 1985 at age 22.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Koblenz, West Germany; father was a civil servant at the revenue service, mother ran a convenience store.
current_position: Active solo artist as of 2025; launched 'Thomas Anders ...sings Modern Talking' project; resides in Germany; net worth not publicly documented.

name: Yuna Kim
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2006 World Junior Figure Skating Championships at age 15, becoming the first Korean figure skater to win an ISU championship. She went on to win the 2009 World Championships and 2010 Olympic gold, all before age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Bucheon, South Korea, Kim started skating at age 5 and competed nationally from age 11, becoming the youngest South Korean senior champion at 12. She won the 2006 World Junior Championships at 15, moved to Toronto to train with Brian Orser, and won the 2010 Olympic gold medal at 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucheon, South Korea to parents Kim Hyun-jae and Park Mi-hee. Family supported her skating from a young age, with her mother encouraging her to continue during a brief period when she considered quitting. The family later supported her move to Toronto for elite training.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in figure skating, but both were dedicated to supporting her training. Her mother accompanied her to Toronto, while her father remained in Korea.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early skating from age 5,dedicated coaching,prodigy talent,family support,limited Korean infrastructure
evidence_summary: Kim started skating at age 5 in Bucheon, South Korea, a country with minimal figure skating infrastructure. She showed prodigious talent early, becoming the youngest Korean senior champion at 12. Coaches Ryu Si-hyun and Shin Hea-sook guided her from ages 10-12, and she later moved to Toronto to train with Brian Orser at the Toronto Cricket Club. Her family supported her training financially and logistically, with her mother relocating to Canada. She won the World Junior Championships at 15, the World Championships at 18, and Olympic gold at 19.
starting_point: Born in Bucheon, South Korea to a middle-class family; father Kim Hyun-jae, mother Park Mi-hee. Family supported her skating from age 5 and her later move to Toronto for elite training.
current_position: Retired from competitive skating in 2014; married Ko Woo-rim in 2022; active as philanthropist and Olympic ambassador; resides in South Korea.

name: Thierry Mugler
milestone_by_age_26: Created his first personal collection 'Café de Paris' in 1973 at age 24, launching his career as an independent fashion designer in Paris.
early_history_summary: Born in Strasbourg, France to a doctor father and fashion-passionate mother, Mugler studied classical dance from age 9 and joined the Rhin Opera ballet corps at 14. He also trained in interior design at the Strasbourg School of Decorative Arts. After designing for London boutiques in the 1960s and freelancing in Milan and Paris, he launched his first personal collection in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born in Strasbourg, France; father was a doctor, mother was a homemaker with a passion for fashion who created her own hats and jewelry. Mugler described a difficult, lonely childhood but credited his mother as his first muse.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was fashion-passionate, creating her own hats and jewelry and personalizing outfits, which influenced Mugler's aesthetic sensibility from an early age.

evidence_summary: Mugler grew up in Strasbourg with a doctor father and a fashion-passionate mother who served as his first muse. He trained in classical dance from age 9 and joined the Rhin Opera ballet corps at 14, developing his understanding of the body in motion. He also studied interior design and designed for London boutiques in the 1960s. By 1973, at age 24, he launched his first personal collection 'Café de Paris' in Paris, supported by fashion editor Melka Tréanton and business partner Alain Caradeuc.

name: Per Nørgård
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the Lili Boulanger Prize in 1957 at age 24, recognizing his early compositional talent. His Symphony No. 1 'Sinfonia austera' was composed in 1953-55 at age 21-23.
early_history_summary: Born in Gentofte, Denmark, Nørgård studied composition privately with Vagn Holmboe from age 17, then at the Royal Danish Academy of Music. He composed his first symphony at 21-23, won the Lili Boulanger Prize at 24, and studied with Nadia Boulanger in Paris in 1956-57 before beginning his teaching career.
family_context_summary: Born in Gentofte, a suburb of Copenhagen, Denmark; father was a tailor. He grew up with an elder brother and learned piano as a boy. He was admitted as a boy chorister into the Copenhagen Municipal Choral School in 1942.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a tailor; no documented family background in music. Nørgård's musical ability showed early through choir training and piano lessons.

evidence_summary: Nørgård grew up in Gentofte, Denmark, son of a tailor, and showed innate musical ability early as a boy chorister in Copenhagen. At 17, he boldly contacted prominent composer Vagn Holmboe for private lessons, which led to formal study at the Royal Danish Academy of Music. He composed his first symphony at 21-23 and won the Lili Boulanger Prize at 24, which funded his study with Nadia Boulanger in Paris. A composer's evening at the Royal Danish Academy in 1956 showcased his work before his Paris studies.

name: Jim Carrey
milestone_by_age_26: Landed his first lead role in a Hollywood production as Skip Tarkenton in the NBC sitcom 'The Duck Factory' in 1984 at age 22, followed by a starring role in the film 'Once Bitten' (1985) at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Newmarket, Ontario, Canada, Carrey started performing stand-up comedy at 15 at Yuk Yuk's in Toronto. After his family fell into homelessness, he dropped out of school at 16. He became a successful local impressionist comic, opened for Rodney Dangerfield at 19, and moved to Hollywood in 1983, landing the lead in NBC's 'The Duck Factory' at 22.
family_context_summary: Born to Percy Carrey, a musician and accountant, and Kathleen Oram, a homemaker. The family struggled financially and became homeless, living in a Volkswagen van. Carrey dropped out of school at 16 and worked as a janitor at Titan Wheels factory to help support the family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a musician and accountant who lost his job, causing the family's financial collapse. The father's musical background may have influenced Carrey's performance instincts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty-driven,early stand-up,prodigy comedic talent,father's musical background,homelessness
evidence_summary: Carrey grew up in a family that fell into severe poverty and homelessness after his father lost his accounting job. He started performing stand-up at 15 at Yuk Yuk's comedy club in Toronto, developing extraordinary physical and impressionist comedic abilities. Despite dropping out of school and working as a janitor, he persisted in comedy, opening for Rodney Dangerfield at 19 and moving to Hollywood at 21. His first lead role in NBC's 'The Duck Factory' at 22 represented a material career milestone, though his true fame came in 1994 with Ace Ventura, The Mask, and Dumb and Dumber.
starting_point: Born in Newmarket, Ontario, Canada to Percy Carrey (musician and accountant) and Kathleen Oram (homemaker); family fell into homelessness, lived in a Volkswagen van.
